column1: # Carrier ledger — retroactive carrier relationships only.
# A carrier commit repeats an earlier commit's subject so that one logical
# change reaches the generated release notes. The two commits are ONE
# release-note change and must consume exactly ONE bullet.
# The NORMAL way to declare that is a trailer on the carrier commit:
#     Changelog-Carrier-For: <full-40-char-sha>
# It is immutable, travels with the commit, and is reviewed alongside it. Use
# it for every carrier created from now on.
# This file exists only for a relationship discovered AFTER its carrier was
# already merged, where the trailer would require rewriting immutable history.
# It is not a general escape hatch: a row here is a repair, and every row needs
# the same proof the trailer needs — both shas resolve, the original belongs to
# the release being assessed, and the two subjects match.
# Format, one relationship per line:
#     carrier-sha<TAB>original-sha
# 849c580  docs: reserve blocked-by for true prerequisites  (PR #502)
#   carries
# 2a88518  docs: reserve blocked-by for true prerequisites  (PR #464, issue #447)
# 2a88518 was committed 2026-08-26T16:19:45-05:00, on a branch opened before
# the v0.19.0 cut and merged after it. It is not an ancestor of v0.19.0, so
# v0.20.0 is its first release — but Release Please stops its walk at the
# v0.19.0 commit (18:58:43) and never reaches it.
